name: *** THE HAMMERSTEIN QUESTION IS ANSWERED, FROM A DOCUMENT ***
record: Standesamt Schubin, Heiratsregister 1874, AKT NR. 9 — the ninth and last marriage of the year. Archiwum Państwowe w Bydgoszczy, Urząd Stanu Cywilnego Szubin Miasto, sygn. 141, "Akta małżeństw - pierwopis nr 1-9", scan 10, read at the image on genealogiawarchiwach.pl on 22 September 2026. SCHUBIN, 24 NOVEMBER 1874. The date the family record has always given, now standing on the register itself.

name: Sally Leibholz
record: *** BORN AT HAMMERSTEIN AND STILL LIVING THERE THE DAY HE MARRIED. *** The entry gives him as DER KAUFMANN SALLY LEIBHOLZ, mosaischer Religion, SIEBEN UND ZWANZIG JAHRE ALT — twenty-seven — GEBOREN ZU HAMMERSTEIN, WOHNHAFT ZU HAMMERSTEIN. Twenty-seven in November 1874 puts his birth in 1847, which is the year this archive has always carried for him and which no surviving register can confirm, Koszalin having stated on 16 September that the Hammerstein books are gone. THE MARRIAGE ENTRY DOES WHAT THE LOST BIRTH REGISTER WOULD HAVE DONE.

name: Jacob Leibholz Senior
record: SALLY'S FATHER, NAMED IN THE ENTRY AS "JACOB LEIBHOLZ", Kaufmann. *** THE SUFFIX "SENIOR" IS THIS ARCHIVE'S, NOT THE REGISTER'S *** — the entry calls him simply Jacob Leibholz, and the word is added here only so he is never confused with his grandson Jacob Leibholz born at Schubin in 1884, who was named after him and who died at Auschwitz. *** THIS IS A GENERATION ABOVE ANYTHING THIS ARCHIVE HELD. *** He is Kurt Luwinski's great-grandfather, and until today no record of him existed here in any form. AND IT EXPLAINS A NAME: the Jacob Leibholz born at Schubin on 8 August 1884, whose birth entry was read the same evening, was named for this man — the ordinary Ashkenazi practice of naming a child for a dead grandparent.

name: Wilhelmine Leibholz née Pollnow
record: SALLY'S MOTHER, named in the entry as his father's wife, "WILHELMINE GEB. POLLNOW". A NEW SURNAME ENTERING THIS ARCHIVE, and the second of Kurt's great-grandmothers to be recovered. POLLNOW IS ALSO A POMERANIAN TOWN — Polanów, Kreis Schlawe — and that is consistent with everything else known about where this family comes from, but the archive is NOT claiming the surname is toponymic on that basis. THE READING OF THE MAIDEN NAME IS THE LEAST CERTAIN THING ON THIS PAGE: it is Kurrent, and P/T/Z are the letters that confuse in that hand. Read at scale as POLLNOW and offered as such.

name: Friederica Schmul
record: THE BRIDE, mosaischer Religion, about twenty years old, GEBOREN ZU SCHUBIN, WOHNHAFT ZU SCHUBIN. So the marriage is a Hammerstein man marrying a Schubin woman IN HER OWN TOWN, which is the ordinary pattern and explains why the couple's children were born at Schubin.

name: # ---------------- WHAT THIS SETTLES, AND IT IS THE STANDING QUESTION ----------------
*** THE SCHUBIN BRANCH IS A HAMMERSTEIN FAMILY THAT MOVED EAST, AND IT IS NO LONGER AN INFERENCE ***
record: Until tonight that claim rested on the Bundesarchiv Gedenkbuch — on the observation that the German centre of gravity of the surname is Kreis Schlochau, and on a family record saying Sally was born at Hammerstein in 1847 which no register could confirm. NOW A REGISTRAR AT SCHUBIN WRITES IT DOWN IN 1874: this man was born at Hammerstein, he lives at Hammerstein, and he has come to Schubin to marry. THE MOVE EAST HAPPENS AT THIS WEDDING.

name: and it closes the loop the archive had half of
record: gedenkbuch-fifty.tsv noticed on 20 September that Sally was born at Hammerstein and married at Szubin, and said the archive "has held both facts for days without drawing the obvious line between them". THE LINE IS NOW DRAWN BY THE DOCUMENT AND NOT BY THIS ARCHIVE.

name: what it does NOT do, which matters for Georg
record: IT DOES NOT MAKE GEORG LEIBHOLZ A BROTHER. Georg was born at Hammerstein on 7 June 1884 and Jacob at Schubin on 8 August 1884, two months apart in different provinces, and two men cannot be brothers on those dates. THAT REASONING IS UNTOUCHED. What has changed is the surrounding probability: the family this archive descends from WAS a Hammerstein family, so a Hammerstein Leibholz is no longer a stranger by default. THE LANES STAY SEPARATE BECAUSE NO DOCUMENT JOINS THEM — but the reason for expecting them to be separate is now gone entirely.

name: # ---------------- HOW IT WAS FOUND, AND ONE MISTAKE ON THE WAY ----------------
the route
record: The portal's person index holds exactly ONE Leibholz, and it is this marriage. The unit's own "Indexes in unit" tab lists all nine marriages of 1874 in plain text, the ninth reading "Marriage act: Sally Leibholz, Friederica Schmul" at PAGE 10.

name: *** AND THE MISTAKE: PAGE TEN IS SCAN TEN, NOT SCAN NINE ***
record: The first attempt took "page 10" for scan index 9 and landed on akt Nr. 8 — Heinrich Gustav Julius Wengatz and Bertha Auguste Albrecht. Stepping back one gave Nr. 7, Carl Lemke, dated 24 November 1874 — THE RIGHT DATE AND THE WRONG PEOPLE, which is exactly the kind of near-miss that gets published as a find. IT WAS THE UNIT'S OWN INDEX THAT SETTLED IT, not more guessing. The rule: when a viewer offers an index, read the index before paging by arithmetic.

name: *** THE MAIDEN NAME TESTED, 22 SEPTEMBER — AND ONLY ONE READING IS A REAL SURNAME ***
record: The reading POLLNOW was offered with an explicit warning that P, T and Z confuse in this hand. IT HAS NOW BEEN PUT TO A LIST OF GERMAN-JEWISH SURNAMES — the Bundesarchiv Gedenkbuch, which holds every name the Federal Archives has reconstructed. POLLNOW RETURNS EIGHT PEOPLE. TOLLNOW returns ZERO. ZOLLNOW returns ZERO. SOLLNOW returns ZERO. Controls either side: LEIBHOLZ 50, and the nonsense string ZQXVWYRK zero, with the Pollnow control re-run mid-sequence and still 8. *** OF THE FOUR WAYS THAT CAPITAL COULD BE READ, ONLY ONE IS A NAME ANYBODY BORE. *** That is not proof — a clerk could have written a surname that no Holocaust victim happened to carry — but it removes the real worry, which was that this archive had invented a word.

name: and where the Pollnows are from, which does NOT fit as neatly
record: The eight: Edith b.1894 GLAUCHAU (Saxony) · Ella Elka b.1869 MEHLAUCKEN · Hans Moritz b.1902 KÖNIGSBERG · Herbert b.1902 BERLIN · Martha b.1875 DARKEHMEN · Michael Max b.1884 BERLIN · Minna b.1871 REUSSEN · Klara Slotowski b.1869 LYCK. *** THE CLUSTER IS EAST PRUSSIAN — Mehlaucken, Königsberg, Darkehmen, Lyck — AND NOT ONE IS FROM POMERANIA OR KREIS SCHLOCHAU. *** Wilhelmine married a Hammerstein man and bore a son there in 1847, so a Pomeranian origin would have been tidier. IT IS A WEAK SIGNAL AND IS RECORDED AS WEAK: the Gedenkbuch is a register of the MURDERED between 1933 and 1945, not a census of a surname, and Wilhelmine herself — born around the 1820s — could never appear in it. EIGHT PEOPLE IS ALSO TOO FEW TO MAP A NAME BY. It is noted because this archive has already caught itself once today reading a hard word to fit a hypothesis, and the honest thing is to say when the evidence does not fit the one it had.

name: and the toponym guess is withdrawn
record: This archive suggested that POLLNOW might be toponymic, from Pollnow (Polanów) in Kreis Schlawe, Pomerania — while saying it was not claiming so. THE GEDENKBUCH DISTRIBUTION POINTS THE OTHER WAY, and the guess is withdrawn rather than left standing as a plausible-sounding aside.
